text:
maya: heads-up: tiny-batch microq-int4 build (horizon-microq-v1) is returning malformed func-call JSONs in the wild. seen ~3.6% parse errors on /invoke vs 0.15% on baseline fp16.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy horizon-microq-v1 (canary=7%) triggered by @maya at 2026-03-23T09:05:45Z

oncall-bot: Alert: parse_failure_rate > 1% on route /invoke/horizon-microq-v1 (canary)

maya: sample (redacted):
```
{"cmd":"attach","args":[{"file":"/tmp/log"}],}

```
alex: trailing comma + blank line before EOF. looks like emission of an extra "," token right after array close.

sam: pattern? nested arrays? code fences? or lightweight replies?

maya: skewed to nested arrays and short codeblocks. also spikes when batch_window_ms is <=8ms.

katie: hypothesis: micro-quant rounding causes slight logit shifts near closing tokens; combined with aggressive batching we sometimes interleave kv-prefix fragments leading to extra punctuation.

alex: can we run a small parity replay (fp16 vs int4) with identical seeds and capture token streams + byte offsets?

maya: started job parity/597831/1k. will capture token-level diffs and streaming chunk offsets.

devex: short-term mitigation options:
- disable auto-repair (we want visibility) and instead snapshot every malformed output
- lower traffic to canary or reduce canary slice until root cause found
- try kv-cache=false for a 1% mirror to check cache boundary effect
- as conservative guardrail: drop continuous-batching for canary (batch_window_ms=0)

maya: agree we should NOT auto-repair yet. snapshotting ON and disable soft-repair. roll kv-cache-off mirror.

deploy-bot: Mirror job queued -> horizon-microq-v1/mirror-kv-off slice=1% by @maya

sam: i'll run kv-cache-off replicate this afternoon and post parse rates. if errors drop, cache boundary is likely culprit.

alex: i'll run tokenizer-probe to compare token IDs and splits across builds; also will produce a small schema-heavy eval (250 prompts) focusing on nested arrays and NDJSON streams.

katie: i'll prep a short internal note for support: explain we're snapshotting malformed outputs and that we intentionally disabled auto-repair to avoid masking issues. keep public comms paused. :zipper_mouth_face: 

oncall-bot: Acknowledged. Will re-alert if parse_failure_rate > 6% or if downstream_arg_mismatch > 0.3%

maya: parity early look: int4 parse_fail 3.4% vs fp16 0.12%. token diffs show an extra token sequence [",","\n"] inserted immediately after array close in ~68% of failures.

sam: interesting. that'll break most strict JSON parsers. also check whether the tokenizer splits multi-byte sequences differently under quantized logits (token ID shifts).

alex: action items:
- alex: tokenizer-probe + 250-schema-eval (ETA 3h)
- sam: kv-cache-off replicate (ETA 4h)
- devex: snapshotting already enabled; keep auto-repair OFF for canary
- katie: support note + dashboard flag (1h)

maya: TL;DR: microq-int4 canary shows suffix-token insertions leading to trailing commas/newlines. guardrail = snapshot+no-auto-repair + kv-cache mirror. follow-ups = token-id probe + schema eval.

alex: i'll post charts when eval finishes.

sam: will confirm kv-off numbers later today.

katie: thanks team. keep any customer-facing fixes on hold until we assess risk of hallucinated args if we ever auto-repaired.

maya: closing for now; will update with parity + kv-off results in thread.
